newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters to strike UPS at midnight.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters to strike UPS at midnight.

text.p: The International Brotherhood of Teamsters will go on strike against United Parcel Service at midnight Sunday, Teamsters President Ron Carey said, saying contract negotiations had broken down.

"We have exhausted every possible approach to solve the problem," Carey told reporters as the union delegation left last-ditch negotiations to avert a potentially crippling strike. "At this point, it's a waste of time ... What that means is there's a strike at 12:01 a.m. (EDT)."

"It's unfortunate, the company has failed to recognise the needs of our members," Carey said. "As a result our membership is prepared and will be prepared as of 12:01 to strike this company," he said.
Carey, a former UPS worker himself, said the union left the talks before the midnight deadline because of "the company's refusal to move."
"To stay there any longer would just be repetition," Carey said. "Somebody's got to stand up and say 'Enough is enough.'"

UPS, the largest U.S. parcel carrier, handles 12 million packages a day and employs 301,000 people in the United States, 185,000 of whom are represented by the Teamsters, including package sorters, loaders and drivers. The Independent Pilots Association is backing the strike and said its 2,000 UPS pilots would refuse work in the event of a strike by package handlers and drivers.
